post.caption: Bog oak jewelry comes from ancient trees. It is oak that turned black after lying buried in peat. Tannins in the wood react with iron in the acidic bog water. Irish bog oak is commonly around 5,000 years old. In 1821, George IV received a bog oak and gold shamrock box. Irish makers sent bog oak furniture to the 1851 Great Exhibition. Designs often copied interlaced patterns from the Book of Kells. Bog oak is so dense that one carver compares it to stone. In one workshop, fresh bog oak dries for four to six years. Bog oak is still carved today, including in County Longford.
